```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant API as ingest API
  participant DB as Postgres
  participant W as worker
  API->>DB: spans stored; root span seen → trace completed (root_span)
  API->>DB: enqueue trace_completed (deduplicated)
  W->>DB: maintenance: requeue stale jobs; complete idle traces (idle_timeout) + enqueue
  W->>DB: claim jobs (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)
  W->>W: load trace → run enabled detectors (pure functions)
  W->>DB: upsert findings, delete stale ones, mark job done (one transaction)
```

{"question": "How does the job queue stop two workers from taking the same job?"}

The job queue stops two workers from taking the same job by using a "SKIP LOCKED" claim. When a worker claims a job, it does so with a "SKIP LOCKED" lock, which prevents other workers from claiming the same job. This ensures that each job is only processed once. [docs/THREAT_MODEL.md]
